manual publication instead of claiming an independent review. This is a separate

independent maintainer approval. This is not branch protection or independent review.

profile from a clean exact-SHA source clone, then publish with the existing
projection publisher. It must record authorization, SHA, checks and resulting
sole-parent commit. Never merge a promotion PR; close it after publication.

# Distribution status

The current installation is the Git-backed main tree, containing independently
installable Skills and the skill-creator Node.js >=22.22.2 launcher/runtime.
See [README](README.md) for installation and [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development.

The pre-migration Bun creator executables, native archives, tagged native workflow
and local staged installer have been retired and removed from current tooling.
No native compatibility or newly published release is claimed by this cleanup.
Historical compatibility evidence and third-party/vendor sources remain retained.

## Unreleased — native keyring verification (ap-44kd)

Version not yet assigned; classify at publication (backward-compatible fix: PATCH).

- **Fix — macOS keyring consent:** Goose-created Keychain items trust only Goose, so
  reading them through `/usr/bin/security` waits for a user consent dialog. The reader
  now allows 60 s on macOS (10 s elsewhere); choose "Always Allow" or export the provider
  variable for non-interactive runs. `security -w` hexadecimal output (non-ASCII
  secrets) is now decoded.
- **CI — native keyring verification:** `native-keyring.yml` writes a synthetic entry with
  keyring-rs 3.6.3 (the library Goose uses) on macOS and Windows runners and reads it
  through the shipped runtime. Windows verified; macOS consent behavior verified.

## Unreleased — frozen host code mode (ap-49tf)

Version not yet assigned; classify at publication (backward-compatible new
functionality: MINOR).

- **Feature:** new evaluation and activation campaigns freeze the Goose code-mode
  setting (`candidateToolModes`); a trial whose private configuration differs fails
  before launch. `activation-run-v1` gains header `candidateTooling` (null for older
  campaigns) and a qualifying limitation; the overview, HTML report ("Code mode") and
  dashboard carry it. The dashboard refuses a delta across known different settings.
- **Evidence:** the Goose 1.57.0 cause and the upstream v1.60.0 fix are recorded in the
  [compatibility evidence](skills/plugin-creator/references/compatibility-matrix.md#unreleased--code-mode-skill-loading-in-activation-trials-ap-qbol-2026-11-20).

## Unreleased — Goose code-mode Skill loading evidence (ap-qbol)

Documentation only; no CLI, option, default or runtime change.

- **Compatibility evidence:** Goose 1.57.0 with code mode exposes no direct
  `load_skill` tool in activation trials (campaign 9c1cef33), although the tagged
  source declares the `skills` extension first-class. Should-trigger activation results
  under code mode are unresolved and only comparable at the same code-mode setting. See
  the [versioned compatibility evidence](skills/plugin-creator/references/compatibility-matrix.md#unreleased--code-mode-skill-loading-in-activation-trials-ap-qbol-2026-11-20).

## 0.10.0 — activation oracle, comparison dashboard, sandbox and keyring credentials

MINOR release before 1.0.0: backward-compatible new functionality and fixes. No
incompatible public-contract change; existing campaigns, grades and exports remain readable.

- **Feature — structural activation oracle:** export attaches an `activation` class to
  selected trials (With: triggered/attempted-failed/direct-read/not-triggered; Without:
  baseline-clean/probe/contaminated; inconclusive for incomplete scans) from the verified
  conversation; the report shows per-condition counts and flags contaminated baselines.
  Scores, deltas and sorting are unchanged (ap-x8p7.3, ap-wxvu).
- **Feature — multi-campaign dashboard:** `scripts/generate-dashboard.mjs` compares at
  least two verified exports side by side; a With-profile delta appears only for
  established comparability (same profile revision, prompt/criteria, judge, host, known
  different configured models). Same-model campaigns are replications, never pooled (ap-r5dg).
- **Feature — opt-in `--sandbox bubblewrap`** (Linux only, `bwrap` required): wraps the
  candidate `goose run`, hiding host `/home`, `/tmp` and `/dev/shm`; network stays shared.
  Sandboxed plans use registry plan schema 4, which older runtimes refuse to resume.
  Not yet verified on a real paid trial (ap-15xv).
- **Feature — baseline-isolation warning:** evaluation warns on stderr when a prompt names
  a profile `<dir>/SKILL.md`; the plan is unchanged (ap-15xv).
- **Fix — regression from 0.9.0:** the private trial environment withheld the desktop
  keyring, so candidate and judge Goose processes using keyring-stored provider keys
  (for example `azure_foundry`) failed authentication. The CLI now reads the Goose
  keyring entry (service `goose`, account `secrets`) with the OS-native store
  (Linux `secret-tool`, macOS `security`, Windows Credential Manager via PowerShell) and
  forwards only the selected provider's absent variables, registered for redaction.
  D-Bus, the keyring itself and unrelated secrets remain withheld; `GOOSE_DISABLE_KEYRING`
  disables the read. Linux reader observed; macOS/Windows readers unverified.
  The forwarded provider key is readable by evaluated code (also under bubblewrap);
  prefer scoped or revocable provider keys.
- **Fix — historical grades** stay readable across judge prose revisions (ap-rcqm).
- **Fix — report viewer accessibility** audit gaps (ap-f1fy).

Version 0.11.0 is published on `main` of `bioinfornatics/agent-plugins` and tagged `v0.11.0`, so the release is complete.

**What I did**
1. **Version bump, PR #102:** changed 0.10.0 to 0.11.0 in 11 files and merged the "Unreleased" sections of `RELEASES.md` into one 0.11.0 section. That section now also covers #96, #97 and #98, which had no release notes. Historical rows in the compatibility matrix are unchanged. Local checks passed, as did all PR checks.
2. **Merge into `develop`:** done as `0680e6e`. The `develop` CI run on that commit passed all 7 jobs and produced the frozen release candidate.
3. **Promotion:** I opened promotion request #103 and ran the promotion workflow in owner-manual mode, locked to the exact `develop` and `main` commits. All three of its jobs (resolve, verify, publish) passed.
4. **Tag:** created the annotated `v0.11.0` tag on the new `main` commit and pushed it.
5. **Cleanup:** removed the `release/v0.11.0` worktree and deleted the branch locally and on GitHub. Nothing in it was left unmerged.

**Checks on the published result**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` | `4854933` → `50f34ec` |
| Only parent of the new commit | `4854933` (the previous `main`) |
| Version on `main` | 0.11.0 (was 0.10.0) |
| Source commit recorded in `distribution-manifest.json` | `0680e6e` |
| Promotion request #103 | closed without merging |
| `v0.11.0` on GitHub | points to `50f34ec`; it didn't exist before |

This is publication under your owner-manual authorization, not an independent review.

**Things to know**
- **Documentation site:** the documentation run on `0680e6e` is waiting for approval of the `github-pages` environment before it publishes. That's a separate flow, so I didn't approve it; the site still shows 0.10.0 until you do.
- **Extra ref pushed:** when I pushed the release branch, the Entire git hook also pushed one of its "checkpoint" refs to `upstream`. That's its normal behavior; I didn't remove it.
- **First commit attempt:** it failed and pushed a branch with no changes, so GitHub refused to create the PR. The second attempt produced the correct commit and PR #102.
- **Tag message:** it doesn't include the line "previous main … is the sole parent" that `v0.10.0` has. The parentage itself is correct, and I didn't move the tag to change the message.
- **Still open:** the ServierHub fork has no `develop` branch, and the `bioinfornatics` account can't push to it. Updating it means picking an account with write access and deciding whether to create `develop` there.
